message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles typically takes about **6 to 7 hours** under normal conditions. The distance is roughly 380–400 miles (≈ 610–640 km) via I‑5 S, which is the most direct route.

### Factors that can affect travel time

| Factor | Impact on travel time |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Traffic congestion** | Heavy traffic, especially near the Bay Area, the Central Valley, or the Los Angeles metro area, can add 1–3 hours or more. |
| **Road construction / detours** | Ongoing projects on I‑5 or nearby highways may slow you down or require detours. |
| **Weather conditions** | Fog, rain, or winter storms can reduce speeds, particularly in the Sierra Nevada foothills. |
| **Stops / breaks** | Planned rest stops, meals, or refueling can add 30 minutes to an hour. |
| **Speed limits & enforcement** | Speed limits vary (mostly 65–75 mph on I‑5), and aggressive enforcement can reduce average speed. |
| **Vehicle condition** | A well-maintained vehicle will maintain higher speeds; a vehicle with mechanical issues may slow you down. |

### Rough time breakdown

| Segment | Distance | Typical speed | Estimated time |
|---------|----------|---------------|----------------|
| SF to Sacramento | ~90 mi | 60–70 mph | 1.5–1.75 h |
| Sacramento to Fresno | ~140 mi | 65–70 mph | 2–2.25 h |
| Fresno to Bakersfield | ~80 mi | 65–70 mph | 1.25–1.5 h |
| Bakersfield to LA | ~120 mi | 65–70 mph | 1.75–2 h |
| **Total** | ~430 mi | 65–70 mph | **6–7 h** |

> **Tip:** Check real‑time traffic apps (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) before you depart. They’ll give you the most accurate estimate based on current conditions and can suggest alternate routes if needed.

If you’re planning a trip, consider leaving early in the morning or late at night to avoid peak traffic times. Safe travels!
